points.quote: HTTP/2 stack | HTTP/3 stack | GET → page
points.problem: The figure and its caption rely on HTTP, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and GET as known, but the book has not yet said what HTTP versions are or what a GET is (HTTP is only deferred to Chapter 11). A newcomer cannot tell what the top box does or why two versions exist.
points.hint: One clause in ch10-modern-p6 saying HTTP is the web's request-and-reply language (Chapter 11) and that a GET is the request for a page.
